catalog.summary: Recording for walkthroughs, podcasts, corporate messages and live feeds, by a person or by an agent.

notes_for_owner: Matches FormRec 0.9.0's desktop build. Version: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json; setup/stage_desktop refuses to build unless package.json, tauri.conf.json and src-tauri/Cargo.toml agree. Build: setup/build_release --target $FORMCOMPILER_TRIPLE on every desktop runner (bash, Git Bash on Windows), taking only aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and passing $FORMCOMPILER_CONFIG_ARG to tauri build. It runs setup/stage_desktop, which needs network to nodejs.org (Node 22.23.4, checked against setup/node-runtime.sha256) and the npm registry (production dependencies, no install scripts, no browsers). Outputs: release-dist/formrec-<version>-{macos-arm64,macos-x86_64,windows-x86_64,linux-x86_64}.zip and release-dist/formrec-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe (NSIS); the Linux zip holds the AppImage. macOS: with APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY the hardened runtime is on, Tauri signs formrec-desktop and the formrec-node sidecar (the Node runtime, which needs allow-jit from src-tauri/entitlements.plist) and notarizes with APPLE_ID, APPLE_PASSWORD and APPLE_TEAM_ID; the script staples every 30 s up to 10 times and checks the unzipped app (Developer ID, team, runtime, allow-jit on formrec-node, staple, spctl, and that formrec-node runs the app). Without the identity it is ad hoc. Windows: formcompiler signs formrec-desktop.exe, formrec-node.exe and the installer through tauri.windows.conf.json, then anything still unsigned in the portable zip. No Python is needed; zip is in linux_packages for the Linux zip. The headless recorder's Chromium is not bundled: Help > Install the Recorder Browser downloads it on first use. macos-x64 is experimental until a first release shows it builds on the Intel runner. Agents: formrec mcp, and the formrec-harness and formrec-skillset skills in .claude/skills. No updater (FormPortal updates), no extras, no assets script; release notes come from the CHANGELOG.md section that names the version.
